newsitem.title: USA: Global computer chip sales rose 3 pct in May - SIA.
newsitem.headline: Global computer chip sales rose 3 pct in May - SIA.

text.p: Global semiconductor sales rose by three percent in May to $11.41 billion, a gain of $331 million from $11.08 billion in April, and increased from the prior year month for the first time this year, according to the Semiconductor Industry Association's monthly survey.

The Global Sales Report showed sales of computer chips gaining 1.6 percent from $11.23 billion in May 1996, with the Asia-Pacific and Americas markets providing the strongest year over year growth of nine percent and six percent respectively.
"May was the best month for the chip industry since April 1996," Doug Andrey, director of information systems and finance for the SIA, said in a statement on release of the data.

"This is a good indicator that the long-awaited recovery is underway," he added, referring to the industry's rebound from a downturn during 1996 in which increased capacity for memory chips in particular pushed prices lower.

Sales in May increased in all four major geographical markets compared with April, the report found, with sales in the Asia Pacific market excluding Japan rising 5.5 percent and in the Americas gaining 3.2 percent on a month-to-month basis.
In Japan, sales hit $2.63 billin in May, up 2.9 percent from April but still 8.8 percent below the year-ago level, according to the survey compiled by the World Semiconductor Trade Statistics group.

Fluctuations in the value of the yen have depressed semiconductor revenues in Japan all year, the WSTS noted. In Europe, sales of $2.38 billion remained relatively flat with both a year ago and from the month of April. The figure represented a 0.3 percent rise from April and an 0.4 percent gain from the year-ago period.
Sales in the Americas hit $3.89 billion in May, up from $3.77 in April and the region's highest total since April 1996, while in May 1996 the region's total was $3.67 billion.
Sales for Asia Pacific, excluding Japan, were $2.51 billion in May, the region's highest total since January 1996.
The global sales figures are based on rolling three-month averages of sales in the world's major computer chip markets.
